risks.title: Persistent Inflation and Higher Interest Rates
risks.summary: Inflation remains stubbornly high, necessitating higher interest rates for longer. This increases borrowing costs for businesses and consumers, potentially dampening economic activity and investment.
risks.watch_for: Core PCE inflation readings, Federal Reserve statements on interest rate policy.
sources: Federal Reserve FOMC Minutes (September 15-16, 2026 Meeting, released October 07 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (Mid-Year Outlook 2026, October 15 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (October Economic Outlook and Key Themes, October 18 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (Looking Ahead, October 16 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Fragmentation and Trade Tensions
risks.summary: Increasing geopolitical tensions and trade disputes are disrupting global supply chains, rerouting trade, and increasing costs, leading to a more fragmented global economy.
risks.watch_for: Developments in ongoing conflicts, new trade policy announcements, and shifts in global alliances.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook, October 07 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment and Economic Impact
risks.summary: Artificial Intelligence is a significant driver of investment and growth, but it also poses risks related to job displacement, control, and potential market overvaluation.
risks.watch_for: Corporate AI investment trends, labor market impacts of AI, and tech sector valuations.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook, October 07 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (2026 SIEPR Economic Summit, October 2026)
World Bank (East Asia and Pacific Economic Update, October 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amidst Shifting Dynamics
risks.summary: The labor market remains historically low in unemployment, but there are concerns about a perceived lack of opportunity and the potential for AI to disrupt jobs.
risks.watch_for: Unemployment rate, wage growth, and AI-related job displacement figures.
sources: Federal Reserve FOMC Minutes (September 15-16, 2026 Meeting, released October 07 2026)

risks.title: Energy Price Volatility and Supply Shocks
risks.summary: Elevated energy prices, exacerbated by geopolitical conflicts, continue to contribute to inflation and pose a risk to consumer purchasing power and economic growth.
risks.watch_for: Crude oil and diesel prices, developments in the Middle East conflict.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (Looking Ahead, October 16 2026)

risks.title: Fiscal Sustainability and Debt Levels
risks.summary: High levels of government borrowing and increasing interest expenses raise concerns about long-term fiscal sustainability and could constrain policy options.
risks.watch_for: Government deficit and debt figures, interest rate trends on sovereign debt.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Outlook for the Budget and the Economy, October 2026)
World Bank (Global Economic Prospects 2026 report, January 13 2026)

risks.title: Monetary Policy Uncertainty and Fed Actions
risks.summary: Uncertainty surrounds the Federal Reserve's future monetary policy path, with differing views on the need for further rate hikes and the timing of potential cuts.
risks.watch_for: FOMC statements, dot plot projections (when available), and speeches by Fed officials.
sources: Federal Reserve FOMC Minutes (September 15-16, 2026 Meeting, released October 07 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for, October 2026)
Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midterms, October 15 2026)
Chase (Are Fed Officials Changing Their Tone Ahead of October's FOMC Meeting?, October 12 2026)

risks.title: Financial Market Volatility and Credit Conditions
risks.summary: While corporate fundamentals are generally strong, pockets of weakness exist, and increased rate volatility and potential shifts in market sentiment could lead to broader credit market stress.
risks.watch_for: Credit spreads, rating migration, and liquidity in leveraged loan and private credit markets.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (October Economic Outlook and Key Themes, October 18 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus that persistent inflation and the resulting higher-for-longer interest rate environment pose the most significant downside risk to the global and US economies. Geopolitical fragmentation and trade tensions are also widely recognized as key risks, disrupting supply chains and increasing costs. While AI is seen as a driver of growth, its full economic impact and associated risks are still being assessed.
